title: Smart Home & Homelab
summary: A self-hosted smart home running 500+ devices on my own servers, with local control and 30% lower electricity use.
details: I designed and built a smart home system covering connectivity, data management, climate control, lighting, voice assistance, and motion control. Everything is integrated into a single app so that it stays easy to use and under local control.
bullets: Used daily by a four-person household, so every automation has to work for people who never open the app
Cut home electricity consumption 30% by automating lighting and heating control, with circuit-level energy monitoring through Emporia Vue and Powercalc
Integrated 500+ smart home devices across Zigbee, Z-Wave, Matter, MQTT, ESPHome, and Bluetooth
Local voice control over the Wyoming protocol, with an OpenAI conversation agent and an MCP server for AI assistants
Scoped and self-hosted photos, media, recipes, and a Minecraft server on Proxmox and Docker, with uptime monitoring, UPS-aware shutdown, and automated backups
Prioritized which services to run by weighing maintenance cost against value
Built my own components when off-the-shelf options fell short, including RoomRelay, mysa2ha, and Russtum Cards

title: RoomRelay
summary: A privacy-focused smart home voice assistant and intercom that runs fully offline on a Raspberry Pi 5.
details: RoomRelay handles wake word detection, voice commands, inter-room communication, environmental sensing, and Home Assistant integration without sending any data to the cloud.
bullets: Offline voice pipeline using OpenWakeWord, Whisper, and Piper
Multi-room intercom with LAN device discovery and a Bluetooth fallback
Sensors for temperature, humidity, air quality, light, and presence
Web dashboard served from the device, plus an optional Flutter companion app

title: mysa2ha
summary: A native Home Assistant integration for Mysa smart thermostats, with no local broker or extra hardware.
details: mysa2ha connects Mysa thermostats to Home Assistant by authenticating with the Mysa cloud, sending commands through the AWS IoT data plane, and polling device state over REST.
bullets: Supports baseboard heaters and mini-split ACs
Exposes climate controls plus temperature, humidity, power, and energy sensors
Discovers devices automatically and installs through HACS

title: Russtum Cards
summary: Custom Lovelace dashboard cards for Home Assistant, including a card for monitoring NAS drive health.
details: A set of custom Home Assistant cards, installable through HACS. The NAS card shows drive bays with live status, a drive health bar, temperature, uptime, and network link status.

title: InfinityCross
summary: An online multiplayer card game: create a room, share the key, and build a grid by making the right guesses.
details: Players take turns choosing a tile next to an existing card and making a guess. A correct guess places the card, while a wrong one wipes a row or column and adds to their score. More adjacent cards mean harder guesses.

title: Game Night Leaderboard
summary: A weighted leaderboard for our board game nights, where wins count for more in heavier games.
details: Wins are weighted by how heavy each game is, and ranked games can award podium points. The site tracks standings, recent games, game champions, and points over time.

title: Russell Corbett Website
summary: The site you're on, and the project I taught myself frontend development with.
details: Built with Astro and Tailwind and deployed to GitHub Pages. I've kept updating it as I've learned more, and it has kept its original look along the way.

title: Engineering Society Website
summary: A hub for all things engineering at Memorial University.
details: The website for Memorial University's Engineering Society, built with Next.js, Tailwind, FeathersJS, and Supabase.

title: Eastern Edge Website
summary: The public website for the Eastern Edge Robotics team.
details: The team's public home on the web, showing Eastern Edge Robotics and its work to sponsors, students, and the MATE community.

title: Engineering One Survival Game
summary: My ENGI 1020 final project: survive Engineering One at Memorial by avoiding fails and collecting tokens.
details: Created as a final project for ENGI 1020, EOS challenges players to survive the difficulties of Engineering One at Memorial. Avoid fails, collect tokens, and try to make it to the end.
